s01-title: Video eight: fail-closed security. Wrong config, and the kernel won't run.
s02-risk: The risk: a superuser bypasses row level security. In Docker Compose, astra is a superuser and astra app is not. One wrong connection string lets tenants see each other's data, with no error.
s03-attempt: We try to start a second kernel as the superuser. It stops with a message that role astra is a superuser, and exits with code one. The guard runs before Flyway, so no migration runs and no DocType is loaded.
s04-guard: For developers: Row Level Security Guard queries the current role. If it is a superuser or has bypass RLS, it throws. The guard is called twice: before the Flyway migration and at startup.
s05-role: The kernel runs as the unprivileged role astra app: no superuser, no bypass RLS, and it cannot create roles or databases. Force row level security covers the table owner too.
s06-live: In the running k three d cluster, the kernel log confirms astra app is under row level security. Kernel, Seata and the CDC worker use non-superuser roles.
s07-honest: To be accurate: a switch, astra tenancy allow RLS bypass, defaults to false. When on, the kernel starts with a warning. Dev machines only.
s99-recap: Superuser or bypass RLS blocks startup. The cluster uses plain roles, and the dev switch is off by default. Next: for developers.
s10-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source, MIT license.
